Interface LocatedHttpRouteBuilder<T>

Type Parameters:
T - The type of the located target
All Superinterfaces:
HttpRouteScope, LocatedHttpRouteScope<T>
All Known Implementing Classes:
DefaultLocatedHttpRouteBuilder
public sealed interface LocatedHttpRouteBuilder<T> extends LocatedHttpRouteScope<T> permits DefaultLocatedHttpRouteBuilder<T>
The builder of the routes of located targets of a type, see LocatedRoutes: besides the routes of an HttpRouteBuilder, whose handlers read the target with LocatedRoutes.locatedTarget(PathVariables, Class), it routes to handlers that receive the target as an argument, of the type of the routes, LocatedRoutes.targetType(). The URIs are relative to the prefix of the locator. 
public void routes(LocatedHttpRouteBuilder<Order> items) {
    items.GET("/items/{item}").handle((request, pathVariables, order) ->
        HttpResponse.ok(order.item(pathVariables.getInt("item"))));
    items.POST("/items").body(Item.class).handle((request, pathVariables, order, item) ->
        HttpResponse.created(order.add(item)));
}

The creators of the builder return a LocatedHttpRouteSpec: besides the terminals of an HttpRouteSpec, whose handlers read the target with LocatedRoutes.locatedTarget(PathVariables, Class), its terminals take a handler that receives the target, after the settings and the body stage of the route. The router checks the target a locator located against the type of the routes it chose for it: a target that is not an instance of the type fails the request, answered by the error routes like a failed controller method. The groups of the routes, see LocatedHttpRouteScope.group(Consumer), are groups of the routes of the same targets: their routes and locators receive the target too.

The error and status routes of located routes are declared in a group, local to its routes: located routes declare no global error or status route, no server filter and no port, which belong to the application routes. Declaring a global error or status route, or a port, fails when it is declared.
